generated_examples.rule: Each source becomes one research-only example. No parcel flood probability, drainage approval, groundwater availability, coastal-delivery state or Future Growth score is inferred.

second_pass_examples.rule: Recheck planning permission, sequential/exception test, FRA, flood-risk activity permit/exemption, ordinary-watercourse consent, groundwater investigation consent and abstraction licence as distinct states.

third_pass_examples.rule: Recheck current Flood Map for Planning, climate-change data, RoFSW July 2026 layers, historic-record incompleteness, dataset supersession, main-river variations and current regulatory guidance.

fourth_pass_examples.rule: Recheck national/strategic map evidence against exact canonical parcel geometry, levels, SFRA, hydraulic model, drainage/outfall, groundwater hydrogeology, coastal frontage and residual-risk evidence. Map overlap alone is never promoted.

extra_examples.fact: Flood Zone 3 and functional floodplain Zone 3b are distinct planning states.
extra_examples.gate: Do not infer 3b from the national Flood Zone 3 layer; use current SFRA evidence.

extra_examples.ref: Long-term area risk versus property event
extra_examples.fact: The long-term service reports area-level risk and says it cannot tell whether an individual property will flood.
extra_examples.gate: Do not convert area risk into certainty for a specific parcel/building.

extra_examples.fact: Flood Zones classify annual probability from rivers/sea and ignore defence benefits.
extra_examples.gate: Flood Zone alone gives no flood depth, velocity or defence-performance evidence.

extra_examples.ref: Climate-change extent versus guaranteed future boundary
extra_examples.fact: The climate-change layer is a composite scenario assuming no future defence or land-use changes.
extra_examples.gate: Treat it as assessment evidence, not a guaranteed future flood outline.

extra_examples.fact: Climate-change allowances are future-assessment inputs.
extra_examples.gate: Do not store an allowance as present-day flood extent or observed level.

extra_examples.fact: Flood storage and defence assets manage risk but can be exceeded or fail.
extra_examples.gate: Asset presence must not be converted into zero residual risk.

extra_examples.fact: Reservoir maps model credible worst-case consequences and do not give failure probability.
extra_examples.gate: A mapped extent is not evidence that reservoir failure is likely.

extra_examples.ref: No historic flood record versus never flooded
extra_examples.fact: Historic Flood Map absence can reflect record limitations.
extra_examples.gate: No recorded outline must not be treated as proof the site has never flooded.

extra_examples.ref: Surface-water model depth versus surveyed level
extra_examples.fact: RoFSW depth thresholds are probabilistic model outputs.
extra_examples.gate: Do not treat a model cell as a surveyed finished-floor or threshold level.

extra_examples.fact: Hazard ratings combine modelled depth and speed.
extra_examples.gate: Hazard class is not certainty that a property will experience that hazard.

extra_examples.fact: RoFSW provides direction of modelled maximum-speed flow.
extra_examples.gate: It does not replace site drainage, threshold and topographic survey.

extra_examples.fact: Model-origin data identifies whether national or compatible local modelling underlies the map.
extra_examples.gate: Model provenance affects interpretation but does not itself determine risk severity.

extra_examples.fact: Updated surface-water mapping expresses overall likelihood bands.
extra_examples.gate: Do not describe it as a forecast of a particular storm or date.

extra_examples.fact: National SuDS standards describe design outcomes.
extra_examples.gate: Compliance intent does not prove LLFA approval, sewer adoption, outfall rights or constructed performance.

extra_examples.fact: Flood-risk activity permitting is a separate regulatory route from planning.
extra_examples.gate: Planning approval cannot be used as evidence that a flood permit is granted.

extra_examples.fact: A qualifying exemption is distinct from a standard-rules or bespoke environmental permit.
extra_examples.gate: Exemption registration is valid only while all exemption conditions apply.

extra_examples.fact: Statutory main rivers and ordinary watercourses have different regulators/powers.
extra_examples.gate: Do not apply Environment Agency main-river permitting rules solely from nearby unnamed watercourse mapping.

extra_examples.ref: Proposed main-river variation versus legal designation
extra_examples.fact: A map variation is proposed until the legal notification/decision process completes.
extra_examples.gate: Do not use a proposed variation as current statutory designation.

extra_examples.fact: Source Protection Zones express pollution risk around drinking-water sources.
extra_examples.gate: SPZ presence is not evidence that groundwater is contaminated.

extra_examples.fact: SPZ designation protects a source but does not quantify spare abstraction capacity.
extra_examples.gate: Do not score water availability from SPZ class.

extra_examples.fact: Vulnerability mapping describes susceptibility to pollution reaching groundwater.
extra_examples.gate: It is not a sample result or observed groundwater-quality dataset.

extra_examples.fact: Older 1:100,000 vulnerability mapping has newer Environment Agency successors.
extra_examples.gate: Prefer the current product and do not mix superseded classes without provenance.

extra_examples.fact: Groundwater-flooding susceptibility is a strategic hazard product.
extra_examples.gate: Susceptibility must not be reported as event likelihood at an exact building.

extra_examples.fact: Consent to investigate a groundwater source precedes any necessary abstraction licence.
extra_examples.gate: Investigation consent does not guarantee a licence, yield or sustainability.

extra_examples.fact: Licence thresholds determine regulatory route.
extra_examples.gate: Being below/above a threshold does not demonstrate sustainable water availability.

extra_examples.fact: Licensing considers impacts and applications can be refused or conditioned.
extra_examples.gate: An availability indication or application is not a granted volume.

extra_examples.fact: A hydrogeological impact assessment informs the regulator.
extra_examples.gate: Assessment completion is not the final licence decision.

extra_examples.fact: RPS368 is an enforcement position for qualifying temporary dewatering.
extra_examples.gate: It does not amend the underlying legal licensing/permitting requirements.

extra_examples.fact: Environment Agency pre-application advice may identify constraints and evidence needs.
extra_examples.gate: Advice is not a licence and may change after detailed evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Shoreline management plans express policy over time.
extra_examples.gate: A hold-the-line or other policy is not proof of funded, consented or delivered works.

extra_examples.ref: NCERM scenario versus future cliff line
extra_examples.fact: NCERM gives erosion-risk ranges under management and climate scenarios.
extra_examples.gate: Do not treat a scenario boundary as a precise future shoreline.

extra_examples.ref: CCMA policy collection versus parcel boundary
extra_examples.fact: National CCMA guidance supports local designation and management.
extra_examples.gate: A guidance page does not establish that an exact parcel lies in a locally designated CCMA.

extra_examples.fact: NPPF requires safe development over its lifetime in flood/coastal-change contexts.
extra_examples.gate: Policy wording alone cannot determine permission or refusal.

extra_examples.ref: Aggregate surface-water counts versus parcel risk
extra_examples.fact: Key-summary datasets aggregate people/property exposure by administrative areas.
extra_examples.gate: Aggregate statistics must not be assigned to an individual parcel.

extra_examples.ref: Planning Data stale flood-zone copy versus current EA map
extra_examples.fact: Planning Data flood-zone records have older collection/new-data dates than current Environment Agency planning-map products.
extra_examples.gate: Use the current EA source for live parcel screening and preserve platform provenance as secondary.

extra_examples.fact: A robust FRA requires proposal-specific levels, access, drainage, climate and relevant flood-source evidence.
extra_examples.gate: No Future Growth promotion until exact canonical parcel geometry is reconciled with current site-specific flood and groundwater evidence.
